## Summary

[[stripe]]'s [[stripe-terminal|Terminal]] reference describes an Android-based smart reader for countertop and handheld use, with customizable checkout UI and internet, LAN, or handoff connectivity. It lists four Terminal SDKs (JavaScript, iOS, Android, and React Native) plus a server-driven integration. The reader reference recommends server-driven when the POS runs on a separate device and offline card collection is unnecessary.

## Software Components (4)

Stripe maintains the reader application, firmware, configuration, and key identifier. The regional tables report reader application, firmware, configuration, and ROM versions. ROM is a separate value, and the rows provide no key identifier.

> [!note] Regional tables and firmware history
> November's regional table lists firmware `1.00.08.01`. The captured firmware changelog ends at `1.00.07.00` dated 2026-09-08, so the release date for `1.00.08.01` is unresolved. The 2026-10-20 changelog entry is for reader app `2.46.4.0`. The combined regional configuration rows do not establish availability of individual models, account eligibility, or S710 cellular deployment. See the [[source-stripe-terminal-setup-reader-s700-s710|separate setup guide]] for model-specific eligibility.

**PCI firmware format**: `STR7x-11-WXYZZ-ABCDD` maps to ROM `W.X.Y.ZZ` and firmware `AA.BB.CC.DD.SZZZ.07`. Both captures give the mapping under Reader software version.

## Updates and Diagnostics

Stripe sends software updates automatically when the reader is idle. Leave the reader on and connected to power for updates at midnight in its assigned location's time zone. The reader restarts at midnight daily for PCI compliance and disconnects from the POS app every morning. An unplugged reader could start updating when switched back on. Reboot to check manually. Missing a required update can prevent payment acceptance.

**Diagnostics**: Settings → admin passcode → Diagnostics. It covers DNS resolution, Stripe connectivity, Terminal events connectivity, Wi-Fi information, and battery and hardware status. In the connectivity troubleshooting guidance, Stripe says the Stripe connectivity test must pass for processing payments and receiving updates.

## Hardware Notes

**Charging and handling**: Stripe recommends 12 W and the supplied adapter. A computer USB-C port must support that level. The guide warns against charging the reader from USB-A. During recovery from deep discharge the LED can be on with the display off for up to 30 minutes. Charging slows outside 15–45°C and stops below 0°C or above 60°C. After liquid ingress, Stripe advises stopping use and letting the reader dry thoroughly before reuse or charging, then replacing it if it still fails to operate or charge.

**LED status**: Both captures list fully charged with power connected, flashing while charging, low (10–20%), critically low (1–9%) or drained (1%), and the reader off or on with power disconnected. The captured tables give the meanings without the LED icons or colors.

**Payment sounds**: Tap success gives one long, high-pitched beep and tap failure gives two short, low-pitched beeps. Chip has no sound. Swipe failure gives two short beeps.

**November device specifications**: Android 10, 5.5-inch display, 4 GB RAM, 64 GB storage, and a 4,950 mAh rechargeable battery. Stripe lists 2.5 hours to charge and estimates 140 hours standby and 15 hours active use, with battery life dependent on settings and deployed features. The table lists USB-C or an accessory dock for charging, Wi-Fi and optional-hub Ethernet, and 4G/LTE for S710 only. Front and rear cameras and microphones are present and unsupported. The audio jack is supported. The security row lists end-to-end encryption, P2PE readiness, and mail order/telephone order (MO/TO) P2PE. See [[source-stripe-terminal-s700-s710-accessories|the separate accessories reference]] for the dock, hub, and case.

## Notable Changelog Items

- Reader app `2.46.4.0` (2026-10-20) lists general fixes. App `2.45.7.0` (2026-09-08) fixes clipped long translated tip text and occasional auto-disconnects in countertop mode. November also adds reader app entries for 2026-05-26, 2026-06-29, and 2026-08-04.
- The November firmware changelog adds `1.00.04.00`, `1.00.05.00`, `1.00.06.00`, and `1.00.07.00` with general fixes. The May reference retains the 2026-04-20 app `2.41.2.0` and firmware `1.00.03.00` entries.
- Reader app `2.39.3.0` (2026-02-24) improves the failed-PIN UI. App `2.38.5.0` (2026-01-13) fixes payment tone volume.
- Reader app `2.33.3.0` (2025-06-30) adds girocard and Cartes Bancaires co-branded card choice on S700. The firmware changelog lists `1.00.00.29` on the same day.
- Reader app `2.31.6.0` (2025-04-29) improves the Cartes Bancaires UI on S700. Firmware `1.00.00.25` (2025-04-28) adds the NFC UID configuration for `Terminal.collectData` and adds Cartes Bancaires support.
- Reader app `2.29.6.0` (2025-03-12) includes an offline SDI fix, PIN sounds, and improvements for server-driven integrations on poor networks.
- Reader app `2.28.3.0` (2025-01-29) includes Doze-mode IoT and handoff fixes. Its pre-insert card entry requires version 2.28 and a Stripe-controlled feature flag.
- Reader app `2.22.3.0` (2024-04-18) adds hidden Enterprise WPA/WPA2-EAP support. The 50% battery requirement entry applies to configuration or key updates while running on battery.

The May capture routes software-acceptance users to the [Terminal bundle release notes](https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/software-acceptance/release-notes.md). November omits that pointer. The two captures leave the status of that separate process unresolved.

terminal-readers-stripe-reader-s700-s710.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/readers/stripe-reader-s700-s710, source-stripe-terminal-s700-s710 summarizes an Android smart reader for countertop or handheld use, with internet/LAN/handoff and customizable UI. The November and May captures list JavaScript, iOS, Android and React Native SDKs plus server-driven. Stripe recommends server-driven when the POS is on a separate device and offline card collection is unnecessary (old raw lines 11-17, new raw lines 12-18). The merchant can run reader diagnostics for DNS, Stripe and Terminal-event connectivity, Wi-Fi and hardware. In connectivity troubleshooting, Stripe says the Stripe connectivity test must pass for processing and updates. Deeply discharged units can show an LED while the display stays dark during up to 30 minutes of slow charge. The merchant should supply the recommended 12W using the supplied adapter or suitable USB-C, with a USB-A warning (old raw lines 48-77, new raw lines 49-78). Stripe supplies automatic idle updates. Leaving the device powered allows assigned-location midnight updates, and the reader restarts daily for PCI and disconnects from the POS app every morning. Rebooting can check manually, and missing a required update can prevent accepting payments (old raw lines 93-105, new raw lines 94-106). The revised summary gives dated May and November software values and restores the four SDKs plus server-driven. The November table now lists reader 2.46.4.0, firmware 1.00.08.01 and ROM 2.2.24.1002, and its hardware table reports S710-only 4G/LTE and estimated battery life (old raw lines 107-121, old raw lines 359-364, new raw lines 108-125, new raw lines 386-407).
terminal-readers-stripe-reader-s700-s710.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/readers/stripe-reader-s700-s710, the revised source-stripe-terminal-s700-s710 records both full captures. May 1 reported 2.41.2.0 / 1.00.03.00 / ROM 2.2.22 and included a separate software-acceptance bundle release-note pointer. November 7 lists 2.46.4.0 / 1.00.08.01 / ROM 2.2.24.1002, adds MX, HK and BG/HR/CY/EE/HU/LV/LI/LT/MT/RO/SK/SI configurations, and its firmware history stops at 1.00.07.00. The October 20 reader application entry and September 8 translated-tip and countertop auto-disconnect fixes appear with their reader app dates. The release date of firmware 1.00.08.01 remains unresolved (old raw lines 107-123, old raw lines 333-339, new raw lines 108-145, new raw lines 357-367). Both captures describe four software components: reader application, firmware, configuration and key identifier (old raw line 101; new raw line 102). Their regional tables give Reader, Firmware, Configuration and ROM; no per-row key identifier is disclosed, and ROM is a separate value (old raw lines 107-115; new raw lines 108-119). The device specs are substantive documentary additions. They give 140 hours standby and 15 hours active as estimates dependent on settings and deployed features. They list front and rear cameras and microphones physically present but unsupported, the audio jack as supported, and 4G/LTE on S710 only (new raw lines 386-396, new raw lines 399-407). The revised battery-link anchor and image asset are navigation/presentation, just as changed table spacing, numbering and punctuation leave existing guidance intact (old raw line 9, old raw lines 19-31, old raw lines 359-364, new raw line 10, new raw lines 20-32, new raw lines 386-415). The Terminal concept retains its reciprocal reader-reference entry and separate model setup and accessories routes. Regional software rows alone do not establish either model's country rollout, and the omitted May fleet pointer does not establish retirement. The page retains the dated pre-insert feature flag and historical NFC UID support (old raw lines 192-196, old raw line 344, new raw lines 216-220, new raw line 372).
